questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: a) 23

questions.question: What does a patent protect? / a). Brand name b). An Artistic work c). Invention d). Slogan
questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: c) Invention

questions.question: India joined the Madrid Protocol for international trademark registration in: a). 2005 b). 2008 c). 2013 d). 2018
questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: c) 2013

questions.question: What is the core idea behind copyleft licensing? / a). Prevent others from using your b). Allow anyone to use, modify, work and distribute the work under the same license c). Keep the source code private d). Allow commercial use only
questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: b) Allow anyone to use, modify, and distribute the work under the same license
questions.final_answer: Option (b) Allow anyone to use, modify, and distribute the work under the same license

questions.question: Which country enacted the first modern Trademark law in 1857? / a). UK b). USA c). France d). Germany
questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: d) France

questions.question: Which Indian law governs the protection of industrial designs? / a). Designs Act, 2000 b). Patent Act, 1970 c). Industrial Protection Act, 1985 d). GI Act, 1999
questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: a) Designs Act, 2000

questions.question: IPR protection helps businesses by a). Increasing labour costs b). Limiting product innovation c). safeguarding their innovations and creative works d). Reducing brabd recognition
questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: c) Safeguarding their innovations and creative works
questions.final_answer: Option (c) Safeguarding their innovations and creative works

questions.question: TRIPS Agreement is administered by: / a). United Nations b). World Bank c). WIPO d). WTO
questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: d) WTO

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of intellectual property? / a). Trademark b). Copyright c). Real Estate d). Patent
questions.solution_html: Correct Answer: c) Real Estate

questions.question: Discuss the importance of related rights and whom they protect.
questions.solution_html:
• Related rights protect performers, producers of sound recordings, and broadcasting
  • organizations-they are crucial for safeguarding creative contributions that are not covered
  • under traditional copyright-these rights ensure fair remuneration and control over the use of
  • performances, recordings, and broadcasts.

questions.question: Write on the rights of the Copyright holder in Literary, Dramatic and Musical works
questions.solution_html:
• Copyright holders of literary, dramatic, and musical works have exclusive rights to
  • reproduce, publish, perform, adapt, and communicate their works to the public-these rights
  • help maintain control over creative output and enable the creator to earn recognition and
  • financial benefit.

questions.question: Compare and contrast the protection offered by patents and industrial designs.
questions.solution_html:
• Patents protect inventions that are novel and useful, while industrial designs protect the
  • aesthetic or ornamental aspects of a product-Patents offer broader technical protection, whereas
  • design rights focus on visual appearance. Both stimulate innovation but serve different creative
  • outcomes.

questions.question: Discuss the role of intellectual property rights in fostering economic growth.
questions.solution_html:
• Intellectual property rights encourage innovation by granting legal protection to creators
  • and inventors-this boosts investment, job creation, and competitive advantage-IPR also attracts
  • foreign direct investment and boosts research and development, thus contributing significantly
  • to economic development.

questions.question: Evaluate the role of Indian courts in shaping IPR jurisprudence with the help of landmark judgments.
questions.solution_html:
• Indian courts have played a crucial role in interpreting and enforcing IPR laws. Landmark
  • cases like Novartis v. Union of India and Yahoo Inc. v. Akash Arora helped define patentability
  • and trademark infringement, shaping a balanced approach to innovation and public interest.
questions.final_answer: and trademark infringement, shaping a balanced approach to innovation and public interest

questions.question: Discuss the benefits and risks of adopting open innovation in R&D- / heavy industries such as pharmaceuticals or software.
questions.solution_html:
• Open innovation enables knowledge sharing and speeds up product development, reducing
  • R&D costs-however, it also risks intellectual property leakage, loss of competitive advantage
  • and coordination challenges-Industries like pharmaceuticals and software must balance
  • openness with protective measures for sustainable innovation.
questions.final_answer: openness with protective measures for sustainable innovation

questions.question: Explain the concept of Copyleft licensing.
questions.solution_html:
• Copyleft licensing allows users to freely use, modify, and distribute software or content
  • provided derivative works carry the same license-promotes collaboration and transparency
  • while preventing proprietary control over modified versions, commonly used in open-source
  • communities like Linux or GNU.

questions.question: What is the objective of the Trade Marks Act, 1999 in India?
questions.solution_html:
• The Trade Marks Act, 1999 aims to protect trademarks for goods and services, prevent
  • misuse or duplication, and ensure fair trade practices-grants exclusive rights to brand owners
  • and helps consumers identify product origin, supporting brand reputation and market integrity.
questions.final_answer: and helps consumers identify product origin, supporting brand reputation and market integrity

questions.question: Discuss on the emergence of WTO
questions.solution_html:
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) emerged in 1995 as a successor to GATT to regulate
  • international trade-provides a framework for negotiating trade agreements, resolving disputes
  • and ensuring fair competition-WTO plays a key role in promoting globalization, reducing trade
  • barriers, and enforcing intellectual property standards globally.
questions.final_answer: barriers, and enforcing intellectual property standards globally

questions.question: Explain how IPR can attract foreign direct investment and promote entrepreneurship.
questions.solution_html:
• Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) offer legal protection to innovations, making markets
  • more secure and attractive for foreign investors-strong IPR regimes encourage technology
  • transfer, joint ventures, and R&D-for entrepreneurs, IPR enables monetization of ideas, builds
  • brand value, and fosters a competitive business environment, driving economic and innovation
  • led growth.
questions.final_answer: Option (d) for entrepreneurs, IPR enables monetization of ideas, builds

questions.question: Analyze how Indian laws align with the TRIPS Agreement.
questions.solution_html:
• Indian IPR laws, including the Patents Act, Trademarks Act, and Copyright Act, have been
  • amended to comply with TRIPS-they balance innovation incentives with public interest by
  • ensuring patentability standards, compulsory licensing provisions, and data protection, thus
  • aligning domestic regulations with global intellectual property norms.
questions.final_answer: aligning domestic regulations with global intellectual property norms

questions.question: Write the importance of PCT.
questions.solution_html:
• The Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) simplifies the international patent application process
  • by allowing inventors to seek protection in multiple countries through a single application
  • reduces administrative burden, provides more time for market evaluation, and promotes global
  • innovation by streamlining the procedure for acquiring patent rights internationally
questions.final_answer: innovation by streamlining the procedure for acquiring patent rights internationally
